narrative.overview:
The console is a hydrological yearbook crossed with a strip-chart recorder. The record itself is the interface: each station is a ruled ledger row, each reading a figure in a column whose head names its unit, and the time axis is a real millimetre grid on paper that runs to a pen-edge "now" line. There are no cards, no KPI tiles, no rounded panels. Sections are separated by rules, and the trust state of every reading is printed on it: a stamp box for synthetic or provenance text, a hatched band for paper where the pen recorded nothing.

The mood is calm, exact and unhurried, a survey office rather than a product demo. Density is ledger-tight. Ink is a deep blue-black on cool chart-paper white; a second blue marks reference values; a single correction red appears only for struck originals, over or alarm conditions and stamps. No-data and unreliable evidence must never resemble a normal reading, so hatch is reserved for exactly those states.

The dark theme is the same instrument at night: a "night chart" of deep blue-black paper with the same pale teal millimetre grid. Status never relies on colour alone; every state carries text, an SVG icon and (when abnormal evidence) a pattern.
keyCharacteristics: Ledger, not dashboard: double-ruled column heads, hairline row rules, figures in tabular monospace.
Millimetre grid (#8fbfb0) belongs only to chart axes; it is never wallpaper.
Hatch (45-degree diagonal line pattern) means NO DATA, UNRELIABLE, FAULT, STALE or UNASSESSABLE, and nothing else.
Square corners (radius 0, at most 2px on text inputs), no shadows, no gradients in the chrome.
Status = text label + 16px square-cap SVG icon + pattern where abnormal; never colour alone.
Stamp boxes (3px double red rule) carry synthetic-data and provenance declarations.
Units live in column heads and beside figures: stage (m), discharge (m3/s), volume (m3).

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Survey Ink carries traces, figures, the active state and every heavy rule. A new accent is a new pen colour; do not add one.

rules.name: The Correction-Only Red Rule
rules.body: Correction Red is for struck originals, over/alarm conditions and stamps. It is never a decorative accent and never a generic "error" wash across a surface.

rules.name: The Grid-Is-an-Axis Rule
rules.body: The teal millimetre grid appears only as a chart time axis (and as hatch strokes). It must never be used as background texture on a page, card or hero.

rules.name: The Unit-In-The-Head Rule
rules.body: A column or axis names its unit (m, m3/s, m3) in its head or label; a figure is never shown without its unit context. Stage, discharge and volume are never merged into one column or label.

rules.name: The Typewriter Figures Rule
rules.body: Every measured number, code and identifier is set in the figures face with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built with rules (double for a sheet or head, hairline for a row) and tonal tint, never with shadows, blur or gradients.

rules.name: The Hatch-Means-Abnormal-Evidence Rule
rules.body: Hatch is reserved for NO DATA, UNRELIABLE, FAULT, STALE and UNASSESSABLE. A chip is hatched only through an explicit data-hatched evidence flag; tone (attention or critical) alone never adds hatch. Normal or merely "not configured" states stay plain.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Synthetic-data and provenance declarations are stamp boxes: 3px double Correction Red rule, Sheet fill, uppercase text, plus an SVG diamond icon.

dos: Do build hierarchy with rules: a 3px double ink rule for a sheet or column head, a 1px Rule for a row, a 2px ink rule to open an h2.
Do set every measured figure, station code and identifier in Cascadia Mono / Consolas with tabular numerals, right-aligned in its column.
Do show status as text + 16px SVG icon (+ hatch for abnormal evidence); give every state a readable label.
Do label synthetic or provenance information with a stamp box and keep the data cutoff in the running header.
Do keep stage (m), discharge (m3/s) and volume (m3) in separate columns or tracks, each with its unit in the head.
Do keep targets at least 24px on desktop and 44px at 36rem and below, with the 2px Plan Blue focus ring at 2px offset.
Do distinguish plain paper ("No 24-hour history supplied") from hatched true gaps.
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients, glass or rounded panels in the chrome; radius stays 0 (2px only for text inputs). The source-map artwork in the Map workspace keeps its own lake gradient and is not part of this system.
Don't use the blue-accent KPI-card dashboard template: no stat tiles, cards-in-cards, or side-stripe accents.
Don't apply hatch to normal, positive, over, under or merely unconfigured states.
Don't rely on colour alone to show a state, and never render a no-data or unreliable reading in normal ink weight.
Don't use the teal grid as a page background or decoration.
Don't introduce a new accent colour or a second display typeface; there is one ink, one reference blue and one correction red.
Don't describe or present synthetic data as real government telemetry.
